components.text: Evil presupposes an objective standard of good.
Objective goodness requires grounding in God's nature.
The existence of evil therefore supports God's existence.
Evil is characterized as a privation that depends on an objective good.
Objective goodness is said to require grounding in God's nature.
The existence of evil is therefore presented as support for God's existence.
Objective truth is independent of human consciousness.
Moral wrongness depends on the psychology of conscious valuers.
A transcendent moral valuer cannot establish itself without circularity.
Moral wrongness is claimed to depend on the presence of conscious valuers.
Inferring a transcendent valuer from morality is alleged to presuppose the being being inferred.
Moral convictions are deeply ingrained and experienced as objective.
Their experienced force gives reason to regard them as genuinely objective.
The moral effect is best explained by a transcendent cause.
Moral rules are experienced as pervasive and deeply ingrained.
The depth of moral experience is offered as reason to trust its objective appearance.
The experienced moral law is said to require a transcendent explanatory cause.
Evolutionary pressures instill a drive toward survival and flourishing.
That drive explains why moral rules feel objective.
Experienced objectivity need not amount to objective moral truth.
Evolutionary pressures can explain why survival-based moral rules feel objective.
Explaining moral experience is distinct from proving the foundational commitment objectively good.
Undirected evolution produces beliefs without a truth-directed intelligence.
An evolutionary origin therefore defeats confidence in any belief.
The defeater applies to naturalistic and moral conclusions themselves.
Evolution is alleged to favor survival rather than truth and therefore to produce unreliable cognition.
The evolutionary account is alleged to undermine confidence in itself and in all other beliefs.
Reason must be assumed as a precondition of any inquiry.
Evolution can explain the emergence of rational consciousness.
Ultimate certainty about reason's reliability is unavailable.
Evolution can explain why survival-based moral commitments feel objectively authoritative.
The foundational commitment to flourishing is assumed rather than shown to be objectively good.
Moral obligation is experienced with exceptional intuitive force.
That intuitive force supports objective moral truth.
Skeptical premises are weaker than the basic moral conviction.
Immediate moral obligation is presented as a properly basic and powerful conviction.
That conviction is said to outweigh the skeptical premises supporting subjectivism or agnosticism.
Evolution is offered to explain moral experience rather than objective moral truth.
The narrower explanatory claim avoids deriving an ought from science.
Moral experience may vary while retaining a common evolutionary basis.
Reason is treated as an unavoidable basic assumption required for inquiry.
Evolved consciousness is offered as a possible explanation of rational capacity.
Ultimate certainty about cognitive reliability is expressly left unavailable.
Moral disagreement alone does not establish moral subjectivity.
Uncertainty about objective facts is compatible with an objective domain.
Evolutionary origins undermine confidence in all resulting beliefs.
Evolutionary origins are alleged to undermine the reliability of all moral and rational beliefs.
Disagreement about moral cases does not by itself disprove an objective moral domain.
Moral ambiguity is offered only as evidence for an evolutionary explanation.
The pattern centers on harm, survival, and disputed classifications.
The argument does not infer subjectivity from disagreement alone.
Reason is treated as a basic practical assumption necessary for any inquiry.
Evolution is offered as a possible source of rational capacity and consciousness.
The con account concedes that ultimate certainty about reliability may be unavailable.
Evolutionary origins allegedly undermine trust in every resulting belief.
Divine design supplies a trustworthy rational capacity.
A rational divine mind provides a non-circular ground for reason.
Beliefs produced through evolution are alleged to lack a trustworthy rational ground.
Design by a rational divine mind is offered as the uniquely trustworthy alternative.
The evolutionary and designed options are treated as an exhaustive contrast.
